payload.prompt: A project lead is deciding whether to connect Azure Language to an agent that routes support tickets by detected language and redacts PII. Which outcomes are valid reasons to do it?

options.text: Combine model reasoning with precise analysis
options.rationale: Correct. With the MCP server connected, an agent can combine model reasoning with precise Azure Language text analysis. That fits routing tickets and redacting personal details.
Correct. Azure Language through MCP gives the agent consistent and predictable text analysis. This is useful when language detection and PII redaction must be reliable parts of a workflow.

options.text: Remove the need to deploy a model
options.error_type: confuses adding a tool with skipping model deployment
options.rationale: The Foundry portal flow starts by deploying a model and saving it as an agent. Connecting Azure Language does not remove that step.
options.better_fit: This does not fit the described setup flow.

feedback.intrinsic: The project may skip the first setup step and never create the agent that will use the language capability.
feedback.instructional: Start by deploying a model and saving it as an agent. Then add the Azure Language MCP server for predictable analysis.

options.text: Force every result to be free-form text
options.error_type: confuses structured analysis with free-form model output
options.rationale: Azure Language is useful here because it supports structured, predictable analysis. Free-form-only results would not fit the need for language routing and redaction.
options.better_fit: This would fit a plain generative reply, not structured Azure Language analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The support ticket workflow may receive loose wording instead of usable language and redaction results.
feedback.instructional: For routing and PII redaction, the value is predictable analysis, not free-form output.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Azure Language through MCP adds predictable analysis while keeping model reasoning.

flashcards.back: An open standard connecting agents to tools and data sources.
The agent or host app that sends requests.
A managed bridge from agents to Azure Language tools.
To give agents consistent, predictable text analysis.
